findings.title: Unsubscribe GET endpoint toggles notification level, so a reload/prefetch mutes the topic
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is reached by a plain GET from an email link, but the body is a toggle: if the current level is above `regular` it is lowered to `regular`, otherwise it is set to `muted`. The request is therefore not idempotent. A user who clicks the email link and then refreshes the page (or whose browser/email client fetches the URL twice, or who clicks the link in two different notification emails for the same topic) ends up fully muted even though they only intended one downgrade. The 301 redirect added at line 102 also makes it easy for the URL to be re-requested. The action should set a single, deterministic target level instead of toggling (and preferably be a POST/PUT with an explicit confirmation).

findings.title: State-changing GET action with CSRF protection effectively disabled
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes persistent user state (`topic_users.notification_level`) on a GET request, and `check_xhr` is skipped for it (line 32). Rails' `protect_from_forgery` does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can embed `` (or a link/prefetch) and silently mute or downgrade the notification level of any logged-in visitor for an arbitrary topic. Email scanners and link prefetchers in mail clients will also trigger it without the user ever clicking. The unsubscribe should either be performed through a non-GET request with CSRF token, or be gated by a one-time signed key embedded in the email link (as is done for the digest unsubscribe key).

findings.title: Nil TopicUser causes 500 in unsubscribe action
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (no `topic_users` row exists for this user/topic — e.g. the row was never created, was removed, or a different logged-in user than the email recipient opens the link). The next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and producing a 500 error page for anyone clicking the unsubscribe link in that situation. The action needs to handle the missing row (e.g. create it via `TopicUser.change`) or respond gracefully.

findings.title: Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, bypassing TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: Setting `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` skips everything `TopicUser.change` does: it does not set `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` and does not publish the `/topic/:id` `notification_level_change` MessageBus message. Two concrete consequences: (1) any open client tab keeps showing the stale notification level, and (2) because `notifications_reason_id` stays `nil` (its common value when the level was never user-set), `TopicUser.update_last_read` will auto-track the topic again the next time the user views it, silently undoing the unsubscribe. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, which will break other mailers
findings.body: `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` interpolate `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Adding the mandatory `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder means any such caller that does not supply `unsubscribe_url` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email fails to send; only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass it (and the message_builder spec had to be changed for exactly this reason). Either make the topic link conditional (e.g. a separate key only appended when `unsubscribe_url` is present) or audit/update every mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe page text claims notifications are stopped even when the level was only downgraded to regular
findings.body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` reads "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." and is rendered unconditionally, but the server only moves watching/tracking down to `regular` on the first visit. At `regular` the user still receives notifications for replies to their posts and mentions in that topic, so the page tells the user something that is not true. The message should reflect the resulting notification level (or the server should actually mute when the message says notifications stop).

findings.title: Unsubscribe link from email silently fails for users who are not logged in
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` filter list, but the link is delivered by email and will frequently be opened in a browser/webview where the user has no Discourse session. In that case `Discourse::NotLoggedIn` is raised and the HTML request is bounced (to the homepage/login) without performing the unsubscribe and without telling the recipient why, so the email's promise "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here" does not hold. Consider a signed key in the URL so the action works without a session, or at least redirect back to the unsubscribe URL after login with an explanatory message.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint or Topic#unsubscribe_url
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (slug redirect, missing-`TopicUser` path, which notification level results, access control for topics the user cannot see) and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` have no controller/model specs. The only test change is passing `unsubscribe_url` into `Email::MessageBuilder` so the existing unsubscribe-link spec keeps passing; nothing asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the email body or that the new endpoint behaves correctly, so the regressions noted above (nil TopicUser 500, toggle-on-refresh) would not be caught.
